item.title: Sophie Cunningham laughs at Stephen A Smith's belittling claim about White NBA players
item.description: Sophie Cunningham says Luka Doncic is "killing it" and calls out Stephen A. Smith's claim that the Lakers can't win with "three White dudes."
item.content:encoded:
Luka Doncic is on pace for one of the greatest seasons in NBA history, averaging just under 40 points per game. WNBA star Sophie Cunningham loves watching him set these records, especially when he makes Stephen A. Smith look like a clown in the process.

This week, Smith again said the Los Angeles Lakers cannot win an NBA championship led by "three White dudes": Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. He said they need more "brothers" to help them.

Cunningham disagrees.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"He’s killing it," she said on her "No Hesitation" podcast about Doncic’s historic start to the season. "He has been so much fun to watch."

"Stephen A. was, like, ‘Why would the Lakers ever build a team around three White boys? Like, look at the NBA history. That’s never going to happen. That’s never going to be successful.’ And he (Doncic) is out there freaking killing it. I think it’s so funny."

Also funny: In the very season Smith is belittling the idea of building around three White players, the Lakers’ trio ranks as the NBA’s best, according to ESPN’s own advanced analytics.

WILL CAIN CHALLENGES STEPHEN A SMITH ON 'RACIST' CLAIM ABOUT 'WHITE DUDES' IN THE NBA

As OutKick explained this week, Doncic, Reaves and Kessler are not the reason the Lakers have only the 10th-best championship odds. Based on their play alone, Los Angeles would be near the top. The concern is the weak supporting cast around them.

Here’s the catch: Those role players are almost entirely Black.

If Stephen A. insists on blaming the Lakers’ championship limitations on a particular race, he’s blaming the wrong one.

The truth can be uncomfortable, can’t it?

Cunningham should laugh at Smith’s statement. It’s laughable. It’s wrong. And it sounds like he’s trying far too hard to appease the people who criticize his coverage of Black athletes.

item.title: Tennessee running back breaks leg in single-vehicle crash, school says, putting season in doubt
item.description: Daune Morris reportedly lost control of his Dodge Charger early Friday, and Tennessee football now faces a College Football Playoff push without him.
item.content:encoded:
A Tennessee football player's season in jeopardy after he lost control of his car and broke his leg in a single-vehicle crash.

Running back Daune Morris, fresh off a big game against then-No. 6 Kentucky that saved the Volunteers' season, now faces doubt on whether or not he will be able to play the rest of the year over something that may have been avoidable.

According to reports, citing records from the Knoxville Police Department, Morris' car hit a fire hydrant and rolled onto its side, while also hitting four other cars.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Morris apparently told police he lost control of his car while making a right turn trying to accelerate early Friday morning. The car, a 2021 Dodge Charger, eventually came to rest on its roof.

He was taken to the UT Medical Center with minor injuries.

The school said Morris suffered a broken leg.

"Tennessee running back Daune Morris was involved in a one-vehicle accident off campus early Friday morning," the school said in a statement. "He sustained non-life-threatening injuries, including a broken leg, and is resting comfortably. We wish Daune the best in his recovery."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The Knoxville News said Morris was also cited last month for speeding and failure to exercise due care as a driver.

Police did not immediately respond to an email from OutKick.

Morris has rushed for 434 yards and three touchdowns this season, including a 66-yard score in the first quarter of last week's 34-6 win over the Wildcats. Tennessee entered the game No. 13 in the College Football Playoff rankings.

The win put the Volunteers at the No. 8 seed in the bracket, and they now undoubtedly control their own destiny to play in the postseason. However, they may have to do it without Morris.

item.title: Connecticut teacher escorted out of school over classroom crucifix heads to federal appeals court
item.description: Marisol Arroyo-Castro says she was escorted out of her Connecticut public school after refusing to remove a crucifix she displayed for a decade, while her school district says the story is more complicated.
item.content:encoded:
A veteran Connecticut public school teacher who says she was escorted out of her school with a crucifix in a box after refusing to remove the religious symbol from her classroom is taking her First Amendment fight to a federal appeals court, with oral arguments scheduled for Dec. 7.

Marisol Arroyo-Castro, who has taught for more than 30 years, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that she was stunned when a school administrator informed her that displaying the crucifix was illegal and warned that refusing to remove it would amount to insubordination.

"I said, 'I can't,'" Arroyo-Castro said, remembering the moment she was told she could return to her classroom only if she left the crucifix behind.

CHRISTIAN TEACHER WAS 'QUITE SHOCKED' AFTER GETTING FIRED FOR TELLING STUDENT SHE'S PRO-LIFE

The confrontation sparked a legal battle over religious expression in public schools, with Arroyo-Castro's attorneys arguing that her personal display was protected by the First Amendment and the school district maintaining a position that prevailed in federal district court.

The dispute began in December 2024, after administrators at DiLoreto Elementary & Middle School in New Britain, Connecticut, ordered Arroyo-Castro to remove a crucifix she had displayed near her desk for roughly a decade.

Arroyo-Castro, who was teaching middle-school social studies, said the crucifix had been a quiet source of comfort throughout her career, something she would look at while grading papers or completing reports.

"I pretty much kept it to myself," she said. "It keeps me calm and [it's] just part of me."

But when administrators pressed her to move it, she said she broke down in tears.

"I just started to cry and cry and cry," she recalled. "They just backed away little by little until they left the room, and they left me there crying."

NASHVILLE SCHOOL PULLS LGBT BOOKS AFTER CHRISTIAN TEACHER WAS DISCIPLINED FOR REFUSING TO READ ONE

On Dec. 11, 2024, she received a formal reprimand for insubordination, and the following day, school officials removed the crucifix and suspended her for two days without pay. She was placed on paid administrative leave on Dec. 16, 2024, and reassigned to a non-teaching role in March 2025.

Arroyo-Castro filed a federal lawsuit in January 2025, alleging violations of her First Amendment rights. A federal judge denied her request for a preliminary injunction in November 2025, finding she was unlikely to prevail because the classroom display constituted government speech. Her attorneys appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, where the dispute over her request for preliminary relief remains the subject of the appeal described in their March 2026 brief.

"They suspended me," Arroyo-Castro told Fox News Digital. "Then they told me that they were going to pay me after that, but that I couldn't go back into the school near the children, that they didn't want me around the students, that I'm not supposed to talk to the students or interact with them or any of the staff in the school. Things like that, like I was a pariah or something."

JUDGE ORDERS WASHINGTON SCHOOL DISTRICT TO LOOSEN LIMITS ON OFF-CAMPUS BIBLE CLUB FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL STUDENTS

Becky Rees Dummermuth, senior counsel at First Liberty Institute, told Fox News Digital in an interview that the case is ongoing.

"So we've appealed to the Second Circuit Court of Appeals, and in the next couple of weeks, on Dec. 7, we'll have an oral argument there in the Second Circuit Court of Appeals in New York City, and we'll argue before the court that Marisol's speech was private speech. And the Supreme Court said in its Kennedy decision a few years ago, made really clear that a teacher's private religious expression is allowable even if students are able to see it."

The Kennedy decision refers to football coach Joe Kennedy having his right upheld by the Supreme Court to pray publicly without fear of retribution.

Dummermuth said that Arroyo-Castro's attorneys will argue her display of the crucifix was protected under the First Amendment's Free Exercise and Free Speech Clauses, adding that public schools must treat teachers equally, arguing that if other educators are permitted to display personal items near their desks, religious expression should not be singled out for exclusion.

VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY ACCUSED OF SUPPRESSING CHRISTIAN STUDENT MINISTRIES WHILE MUSLIM GROUPS ARE EXEMPT

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Consolidated School District of New Britain said, "The Consolidated School District of New Britain has consistently maintained that this matter extends beyond the presence of a religious symbol in a classroom. As outlined in the attached independent, third-party investigative report, the district's concerns involved a broader pattern of statements and actions that raised serious concerns about the treatment of students of differing religious backgrounds."

The spokesperson continued, "The district respects the religious beliefs and individual rights of all students and staff. However, we also have a legal and ethical responsibility to ensure that every classroom remains an inclusive and welcoming environment where students of all faiths and backgrounds feel respected and valued."

The spokesperson added, "Throughout this process, we have operated in good faith and provided multiple options to Ms. Castro, which she and her attorneys have declined. Ms. Castro was offered a variety of ways in which she could practice her faith while not encroaching on the religious freedoms of her students. 

"She declined all of the options that were provided to her. We will continue to follow legal guidance as we move forward, and we remain steadfast in our duty to uphold both the law and the values of inclusion, neutrality, and respect for all of our students and families."

The district's referenced third-party report obtained by Fox News Digital included interviews with four teachers and the school's principal and assistant principal, as well as Castro herself. It also reiterated several students' claims that she referenced God, Jesus and religion in a matter the investigator concluded was inappropriate. It included Castro's denial that she made such references "during a class."

The teachers interviewed in the report also criticized Castro's classroom management and treatment of students.

First Liberty responded, "The school district repeatedly told Ms. Castro that she could return to the classroom if she simply took down the crucifix. When they removed her from the classroom, the only concern they mentioned was preventing an alleged Establishment Clause violation, a baseless concern that cannot survive the Supreme Court’s Kennedy decision."

item.title: ‘Saved by the Bell’ star Tiffani Thiessen says she needs hip replacement at 52 after painful diagnosis
item.description: Tiffani Thiessen revealed a torn labrum and hip dysplasia diagnosis on a podcast, joking she's "basically a German shepherd" ahead of hip replacement.
item.content:encoded:
Tiffani Thiessen's active lifestyle hit a painful roadblock after the "Saved by the Bell" star learned she was dealing with more than just the usual aches and pains.

The 52-year-old actress shared her diagnosis and revealed she has to have a hip replacement during an appearance on the podcast "Breaking Bread with Tom Papa."

"I was a dancer when I was younger, which was a good thing," Thiessen explained. "I have a torn labrum. That's one issue I have."

"This is what happens. Just wait. You guys just wait," she jokingly warned. "And then I found out going to my second opinion that I'm basically a German shepherd. I have hip dysplasia."

'SAVED BY THE BELL' STAR TIFFANI THIESSEN 'FELL IN LOVE' WITH ICE PLUNGING

Thiessen claimed her flexibility as a child, which helped her to dance, might have caused her hip issues.

"I hear that hip replacements aren't as bad as knee and shoulder," she added.

Thiessen's painful condition eventually forced her to put one of her favorite pastimes on hold.

"My doctor didn't say it was pickleball, but it probably hasn't helped," she admitted. "I have not been able to play in the last couple weeks because my hip's been so bad."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Thiessen often plays alongside her son, who started playing less than a year ago.

"He's actually starting to beat me now. But I do have a bad hip," she emphasized.

While Thiessen's hip problems forced her to slow down physically, the actress showed no signs of wanting to step away from Hollywood.

Thiessen began modeling and appearing in commercials as a child, winning the Miss Junior America title in 1987. Her big break came in 1989 when she landed the role of Kelly Kapowski on "Saved by the Bell." The character quickly became a fan favorite, helping establish Thiessen as a teen idol.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Decades after becoming a household name, Thiessen revealed that her biggest career goal had little to do with fame or recognition.

"It's more just wanting to continue to have the opportunity to do it," she said. "That's what it is for me now. It's not so much specific – I want this or this award or this type of film or work with this type of person. I mean, I have a lot of those."

"But, it's more, the main thing is just getting to still do it," Thiessen added. "As we get older, that starts to get smaller. And so the fact that I get to still do what I love is really what is most important to me."

In 1994, she joined the cast of "Beverly Hills, 90210" as the scheming Valerie Malone, demonstrating her ability to move beyond wholesome teenage roles.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

While Thiessen acknowledged the challenges of getting older in Hollywood, she credited a new generation of actors with helping her maintain a youthful outlook.

"I've been very lucky with most of the projects that I've done have either been successful or just really great to do," she said during the podcast. "I really like working with this young generation. Like they just, they're really fun.

"I think they're keeping me young," she added. "Like, you know, four o'clock in the morning, the mom is like, 'Oh my God, how many more scenes?' And these kids are over there doing TikToks."

Thiessen stars as Miss Graves, the head of a supernatural boarding school for young witches and warlocks, in "Coven Academy." She also recently voiced the superhero She-Hulk in the animated special "LEGO Marvel Avengers: Mission Demolition" in 2024.

item.title: 5 of the unluckiest plays in sports history to revisit in honor of Friday the 13th
item.description: From Leon Lett's Super Bowl fumble to the Kick Six, these five unlucky plays prove Friday the 13th has nothing on sports history's cruelest moments.
item.content:encoded:
Friday the 13th. A day synonymous with bad luck and people who genuinely believe walking under a ladder might ruin their entire existence.

Over the centuries, sports have proven a twisted sense of humor. Bad luck runs rampant. You can practice your entire life to hone your skills, execute a play almost perfectly, and still end up on the wrong side of a moment so ridiculously unfortunate that it feels like someone upstairs is playing a practical joke.

And in honor of Friday the 13th, we're counting down five of the most unlucky, bizarre and downright cruel plays in sports history.

DUKE'S BEATDOWN OF NC STATE INCLUDED A MUST-SEE MISSED FIELD GOAL RETURNED FOR A 109-YARD TOUCHDOWN

Imagine being the No. 1 team in college football, having national championship aspirations and watching your season take a devastating turn because of a missed field goal.

Welcome to Alabama's nightmare.

With the 2013 Iron Bowl tied at 28 and just one second remaining, Nick Saban sent freshman kicker Adam Griffith onto the field to attempt a 57-yard field goal against Auburn.

What could possibly go wrong?

Griffith's kick fell short, landing in the hands of Auburn's Chris Davis, who was standing in the end zone specifically for this possibility.

Davis proceeded to sprint 109 yards for a touchdown as the Auburn crowd erupted into absolute pandemonium and stormed the field.

The Crimson Tide didn't just lose a football game. They watched their hopes of a third consecutive national championship disappear as Davis sprinted down the sideline.

For 86 years, the Boston Red Sox couldn't win a World Series.

And for a long time, their fans blamed a certain trade involving a certain baseball player with certain significance, named Babe Ruth.

The infamous "Curse of the Bambino" had become part of Boston sports folklore, and the 1986 World Series provided perhaps its cruelest chapter of that saga.

Leading the New York Mets 3-2 in the series, Boston was one out away from winning its first championship since 1918 during Game 6.

Then everything fell apart.

The Mets tied the game in the 10th inning, and with the winning run on second base, Mookie Wilson hit a slow ground ball toward Red Sox first baseman Bill Buckner.

It should have been a routine play. Instead, the baseball rolled directly between Buckner's legs, allowing Ray Knight to score the winning run.

Game over.

The fat lady had sung. The Mets won Game 7, and Buckner's error became one of the most infamous moments in baseball history.

To be fair, Boston had already blown its lead before Buckner's mistake, and the Red Sox still had another game to win the championship, but whether you want to call it poor concentration or bad luck, it's one of the most brutal plays you'll ever watch, unless you're a Yankees or Mets fan.

YANKEES INFIELDERS COLLIDE, ALLOWING METS TO SCORE GAME-WINNING RUN IN DRAMATIC COMEBACK

There are missed field goals.

There are heartbreaking missed field goals.

And then there's whatever supernatural, if you will, nonsense happened to Chicago Bears kicker Cody Parkey during the 2018 NFL playoffs.

On Jan. 6, 2019, the Bears trailed the Philadelphia Eagles 16-15 in the final seconds of their NFC Wild Card matchup.

Parkey lined up for a 43-yard field goal that would send Chicago into the divisional round.

The kick went up.

DOINK.

The football struck the left upright.

DOINK.

Then it bounced off the crossbar, falling into the end zone.

The Bears' season was over.

To make matters even more painful, Eagles defensive lineman Treyvon Hester had gotten a fingertip on the football, meaning the kick was officially ruled blocked.

Parkey had already hit the uprights four times in a single game earlier that season, making this an almost comically cruel conclusion.

One doink is unfortunate. Two doinks on the same kick, with your season hanging in the balance is about as unlucky as you can get.

VANDERBILT PULLED OFF THE MOST IMPROBABLE LAST-SECOND VICTORY YOU'LL EVER SEE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL

If Friday the 13th had an official baseball highlight, this would be it.

On May 26, 1993, Texas Rangers' outfielder José Canseco was tracking a deep fly ball hit by Cleveland's Carlos Martínez.

Canseco drifted back toward the warning track, positioned himself near the wall and prepared to make what appeared to be a fairly ordinary defensive play.

Instead, the baseball struck him directly on the noggin and sailed over the outfield fence for a home run.

Canseco didn't just fail to make the catch. He somehow transformed a fly ball into one of the most embarrassing home runs in MLB history.

It was comical and unlucky at the same time.

Canseco got one baseball to the dome and a lifetime of internet humiliation.

There are few things more embarrassing than celebrating a touchdown before actually scoring it. We've seen far too many bonehead plays where players drop the ball before the goal line.

Just ask former Dallas Cowboys defensive lineman Leon Lett.

During Super Bowl XXVII against the Buffalo Bills, Lett recovered a fumble and began rumbling toward the end zone for what appeared to be an easy defensive touchdown.

The Cowboys were already dominating the Bills, and Lett was about to add another six points to the scoreboard. It would have been his lone touchdown in his career.

There was just one tiny problem. He forgot that the play wasn't over.

As Lett approached the goal line, he slowed down and began holding the football away from his body in celebration.

Meanwhile, Buffalo receiver Don Beebe sprinted after him like his life depended on it, caught Lett just before the goal line and knocked the football out of his hand. The ball rolled through the end zone for a touchback.

Lett went from Super Bowl glory to an all-time blooper.

The good news? Dallas still won the game 52-17.

The bad news? More than three decades later, people still remember the defensive lineman who managed to fumble away a touchdown while celebrating it.

And as if the football gods weren't finished tormenting him, Lett became the central figure in another bizarre play later that year when he touched a blocked field goal in the snow against the Miami Dolphins, allowing Miami to recover and eventually kick the game-winner.

Two legendary football blunders in one calendar year? Yikes.

Sports are supposed to reward preparation, execution and talent. But every once in a while, the sports gods decide to throw a wrench into that equation.

Happy Friday the 13th, sports fans. Watch out for black cats, avoid walking under ladders and, whatever you do, hold onto the football until you're actually in the end zone.

item.title: Severe allergic reaction after sipping energy drink traced to unexpected source
item.description: A teen's severe allergic reaction to an energy drink was traced to cod collagen, revealing how fish-derived ingredients can hide in unexpected products.
item.content:encoded:
Anaphylaxis – a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction – is usually tied to peanuts or shellfish, but a recent case has brought up a new concern.

According to a report by the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (ACAAI), a teen experienced a severe allergic reaction from an energy drink.

The case, which was presented at the ACAAI’s 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting held Nov. 12–16 in Phoenix, Arizona, involved a 15-year-old boy who developed "widespread hives," wheezing and difficulty breathing after trying a new beverage.

POPULAR DRINKS LINKED TO HEART ATTACKS, CARDIAC ARREST IN YOUNG ADULTS, STUDY FINDS

The teen was reportedly taken to the hospital, where he received two doses of epinephrine, albuterol — a medication commonly used in rescue inhalers to help open the airways — an antihistamine and IV fluids. His symptoms resolved after treatment.

A review of the drink’s label revealed that it contained 5 grams of collagen derived from cod.

According to the report, the teen reported mild throat itching and lip swelling when eating canned tuna, although he had eaten salmon without an issue. He also has eczema, asthma and allergic rhinitis (commonly called hay fever).

WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD

Despite the teen's symptoms, a skin prick testing for tuna, cod and flounder allergy all returned negative.

These findings represent initial research presented at the ACAAI conference, and have not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

Allergist Annabelle Rowland, M.D., study author and ACAAI member based in Georgia, commented in a news release that this case shows "how tricky fish allergy can be."

"Collagen from fish is showing up in a growing number of products, from drinks to supplements," she said. "Standard fish allergy tests mostly look for a different fish protein and contain very little collagen, so a person can test negative and still react."

In a statement sent to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Council for Responsible Nutrition in Washington, D.C., said that collagen ingredients can come from several animal sources, like fish, cattle and pigs.

"While collagen has been studied for potential benefits related to skin and joint health, consumers should consider their individual health needs and sensitivities when choosing products," they advised.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Fish-derived collagen can pose an allergy risk for people sensitive to fish, and processing or hydrolysis does not necessarily eliminate that risk."

The spokesperson recommended those with fish allergies should carefully review product labels, which are required to identify major food allergens, such as fish. Consumers should also consult with their healthcare provider before considering these products.

"The case presented at ACAAI highlights the importance of allergen awareness, but a single suspected reaction does not establish how frequently such reactions occur," they added.

"Product manufacturers are required by law to provide accurate ingredient information and major allergen disclosures so consumers can make informed choices."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Sung Poblete, Ph.D., CEO of Virginia-based Food Allergy Research & Education, told Fox News Digital that fish collagen is increasingly being used in products like supplements, beverages and wellness items.

"While many people with fish allergy avoid all finned fish, reactions can vary between individuals and between different fish-derived proteins," she said. "So someone can be allergic to one type of fin fish and not another."

Poblete added that labels must identify the species of fish. Crustacean shellfish, such as shrimp, crab and lobster, must also be specifically identified, according to the FDA.

"For someone managing fish or shellfish allergy, 'marine collagen' on a label calls for a closer look at the ingredient list and 'contains' statement," she said. "If the source still isn’t clear, FARE encourages people to call the manufacturer before using the product."

Consumers are encouraged to ask the manufacturer what the collagen is made from, and how the product is sourced, packaged and tested for allergens.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This case offers a timely reminder to read every label, including on drinks and supplements, and talk with an allergist about any reaction, even if a test came back negative," Poblete added.

Fox News Digital reached out to energy drink manufacturers for comment.

item.title: Is it weird for a coach to not talk to his team after a game, or is it extremely weird?
item.description: Auston Matthews revealed that Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller doesn't usually talk to the team after games, raising eyebrows as Toronto sits 8-11-2.
item.content:encoded:
There are some things in sports that I thought were completely universal to the point that I never even think about them. One of them is a coach talking to their team after a game.

I had assumed this happened about 99.99% of the time. Sure, you might occasionally get the cold shoulder after an abysmal effort to send a message, but that's still communication.

However, an NHL bench boss is getting some attention after one of his players revealed that he normally doesn't talk to the team after games.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews addressed the media after his team's 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday, and that's when he said that head coach Jim Hiller doesn't usually talk to the team after games.

"He usually doesn’t speak after games, so I’m sure we’ll continue to try to clean some stuff up, go over video and make adjustments," Matthews said. "At the end of the day, it’s just minimizing those big mistakes or turnovers, especially against other teams’ top lines."

Uhh... I didn't realize that was optional.

Not even a "Good effort tonight, boys," when things are cooking, or a "You dopes are going to be bag skating tomorrow," after a brutal loss?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I literally can't picture this happening in the NFL. Imagine if after a game they did the requisite cut to the locker room and everyone was just sitting around taking off their pads and shooting their game jerseys into the laundry bin because the coach was like, "Meh, I'm not talking."

I would find it awkward not to say something.

Coaching is all about communication, and not talking to the fellas after a game seems like an odd approach.

But hey, if it's working then... oh, it's not working.

This tidbit of info is not one that earned Hiller many fans, as the Leafs — always under the microscope as they are — are 8-11-2 on the year and sitting in seventh place in the Atlantic Division.

Now, some post-game platitudes aren't going to win you games... but it also won't get the fans on your side when wins are tough to come by.

item.title: Tanker slams into docked New Orleans river cruiser carrying 129 passengers, sparking rescue
item.description: The Atlantic Asphalt tanker slammed into the docked American Heritage cruise ship on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
A tanker slammed into a docked river cruiser carrying about 129 passengers in New Orleans Friday, triggering rescue operations as emergency crews brought passengers ashore for triage and assistance.

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage around 12:30 p.m. on the Mississippi River, the Port of New Orleans said in a statement shared with Fox News. Crew members were also aboard the cruise ship.

University Medical Center New Orleans and other LCMC Health hospitals received an estimated two dozen patients following the incident, LCMC Health said in a statement. Medical teams were evaluating patients and providing care while coordinating with emergency responders.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the Coast Guard was supporting state and local responders near mile marker 96 on the Mississippi River.

"We are throwing every asset we have to help rescue missing passengers," Mullin wrote on X, adding that DHS was coordinating closely with Louisiana officials. "Our prayers are with all those impacted by this terrible tragedy."

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

The Coast Guard said the Mississippi River was closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 while responders assessed the situation and conducted response operations.

American Cruise Lines confirmed that guests and crew were evacuated and said it was coordinating closely with the U.S. Coast Guard and local authorities.

"Guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned for everyone involved," the company said in a statement. "We will share more information as it becomes available." 

The United Cajun Navy said on X that it was on standby at the port.

The New Orleans Fire Department and NOLA Ready said in a Facebook update that multiple people had been rescued and search-and-rescue operations were ongoing at the time of the post.

"Public safety agencies are coordinating response efforts, with the immediate priority being the safety and rescue of those involved," the update said.

The number of injuries and the cause of the collision have not been confirmed, port officials said.

"Our immediate priority is the safety of all passengers, crew members and first responders," the port said. "This remains an active and evolving incident."

Acadian Ambulance said on X that it had transported eight patients and had 15 units and two sprint trucks on scene to assist New Orleans EMS and other first responders. The ambulance service said it was prepared to send additional units if needed.

Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, the U.S. Coast Guard and emergency medical personnel were on scene conducting rescue and response operations.

AT LEAST 40 RESCUED, 2 DEAD AS BOAT CAPSIZES AFTER MACHETE FIGHT NEAR PUERTO RICO

Passengers were being brought inside the Port of New Orleans Administration Building for triage and assistance, officials said.

The American Heritage had docked about two hours before the collision to begin letting passengers off.

According to the news release, skies were clear with no precipitation around the time of the collision, with temperatures in the upper 60s and north winds of 8 to 12 mph, gusting to 15 to 17 mph. The release listed the current water temperature at around 66 degrees.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said he was heading to New Orleans as authorities responded.

"We are aware of the incident on the Mississippi and we are in close contact with local officials and law enforcement," Landry wrote on X. "I am headed to New Orleans now."

Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., said he was closely monitoring the response.

"I am devastated to hear about the ships crashing near the Port of New Orleans," Carter wrote on X. "I am monitoring the situation closely and praying for the swift rescue of survivors and for all emergency crews responding to the situation."

Rep. Julia Letlow, R-La., also offered prayers for passengers and first responders.

"Praying for a successful rescue mission by the dedicated first responders on the scene near the Port of New Orleans, and for the health and safety of all passengers affected," Letlow wrote on X.

NOLA Ready, the city’s emergency preparedness agency, urged people to avoid the area and allow responders to work.

item.title: Former CIA Director John Brennan's son arrested after FBI uncovers dozens of alleged child porn images
item.description: Kyle Brennan, 40, son of former CIA Director John Brennan, was arrested on a federal child pornography charge after an FBI investigation, prosecutors say.
item.content:encoded:
The son of former CIA Director John Brennan was arrested for allegedly possessing child pornography, Fox News has learned.

Kyle Brennan, 40, was charged with transportation of child pornography, according to a federal complaint.

The case originated when Adobe CyberTipline reports flagged accounts linked to Brennan for uploading illicit files involving minors. 

In April and June 2024, Adobe submitted two reports to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) regarding an account allegedly used to upload suspected child sexual abuse material.

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS BLUE STATE'S LAW PROHIBITING ICE AGENTS FROM WEARING MASKS ON THE JOB

The FBI's Washington field office is involved in the investigation.

Around April 7, 2024, three files were uploaded to the Adobe account. A review of the files indicated a file that appeared to be a morphed image combining the face of a minor girl, later identified as a 12-year-old, with the naked body of another minor, federal prosecutors said. 

Comcast records showed that the IP address used to upload the files was registered to Kyle Brennan at an address in Warrenton, Virginia, where he lives.

Records from Apple later confirmed that the private relay account was registered to Brennan, authorities said. 

DOJ LAUNCHES GRAND JURY PROBE INTO MARXIST MOGUL NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S FUNDING OF LEFTIST GROUPS

In July 2024, authorities searched Brennan's home and seized his iPhone. 

The case was referred to the FBI in October, and a judge signed off on a warrant so investigators could examine the records and seize Brennan's phone. 

On Friday, an FBI analysis of the iPhone, which was named "Kyle’s iphone (2)" contained a photograph of Brennan’s Virginia driver’s license and revealed approximately 88 images depicting girls under the age of 18 engaged in sexually explicit conduct, prosecutors said. 

One image appeared to be a "fully nude, pubescent minor girl on a locker bench," the complaint states. 

"The girl’s wrists and ankles were bound and her mouth was gagged," it said. 

The Justice Department is investigating John Brennan, who served under former President Barack Obama, regarding his role in the 2017 Intelligence Community Assessment (ICA) on Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election.

Fox News Digital has reached out to a representative for John Brennan and the Justice Department for comment.

item.title: Curt Cignetti taunts the CFP committee and then gets obliterated, Cam Skattebo freezes & Gracie Hunt checks in
item.description: Curt Cignetti fires back at the CFP committee over Indiana's five-spot drop, but fans were quick to point out the Hoosiers' zero ranked wins.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Well, here we are. Friday. We've made it!

The weather man tells me we're supposed to drop down to the 40s tonight here in Florida. We've got a full weekend of FOOTBALL in front of us. Thanksgiving is 13 days away.

I missed a meeting yesterday because Outlook was broken and I couldn't access the calendar with the Zoom link. What a pleasure.

Who has it better than us right now? Nobody! We're rolling.

Let's get after it.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Curt Cignetti fires SHOTS at the CFP committee, and then promptly takes on heavy fire from fans in the comments section.

HERE'S HOW BAD THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF'S SELECTION COMMITTEE RANKINGS ACTUALLY ARE | IAN MILLER

Lordy, these rankings are divisive. Good thing we're expanding!

What else? I've got plenty of reader mail from the week to get to now that my email is no longer under a cyberattack (allegedly!), and did Cam Skattebo cost the Giants the game last night?

I know I know — he scored twice. But did y'all see what he did, or didn't do, on that third down play late in the fourth quarter? Wild. We'll dive in.

Grab you a sweatshirt if you're down here in FRIGID Florida, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

It's a Friday and we've got a lot to get to, so let's get this class started and see if we can get outta here a few minutes early ...

Once again, a Big Ten coach has the SEC on his mind. Last weekend, it was Illinois' Brett Bielema, who said his team would be ranked in the top-15 if they were in the SEC.

It's a fair point until you remember that Bielema went ... checks notes ... 11-29 in the SEC over his five seasons at Arkansas. That's a tough sell.

WE NEED TO ABOLISH THE CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE AFTER YET ANOTHER EMBARRASSMENT | IAN MILLER

The latest shot at the committee came from defending champ Curt Cignetti, who certainly has more street cred than Beilema. When Cig talks, folks listen. Doesn't mean he's right, but they at least don't laugh.

Here's what Cignetti had to say after the Hoosiers dropped five spots in this week's rankings even though they were on a bye week:

"Bad losses don't count anymore? 😂😂😂😂😂😂 Are first downs still 10 yards?🤡🤡🤡"

Thoughts? Look, I don't know who, exactly, Cignetti is singling out here. No. 1 Georgia, which lost to an unranked Auburn team a few weeks ago? No. 6 Texas? The Longhorns have lost to Florida (yuck) and Oklahoma (double yuck). Either way, it's an SEC team.

Here's the problem ... Indiana hasn't exactly faced a gauntlet this season. The Hoosiers have one loss — against Ohio State — and needed overtime to beat Michigan and Minnesota.

The SEC is just better than the Big Ten this year ... by a lot. It's a down year for the Big Ten. It happens. The committee is almost certainly punishing Indiana for the schedule compared to Texas or Georgia. Fair or not, that's what they're doing.

The always levelheaded folks on social media were QUICK to point that out:

Yeah, it's just a tough look to chirp and also have zero ranked wins this season. Zero. That could very well change tomorrow as Indiana faces No. 18 USC.

I assume the Hoosiers will win that game because USC under Lincoln Riley never meets the moment. Ever. But should they lose? It'll be open season when the next batch of rankings come out next week.

OK, let's leave Bloomington and head to New Jersey, where the Giants lost a game they should've won last night partly because Cam Skattebo appeared to ... do nothing? ... on a critical third down QB sneak:

I watched it live and was truly baffled. What in the world is going on here? Some folks on the internet think Skattebo was a decoy. OK? That still doesn't explain why he just sat there for two seconds while Jameis was fighting for his life trying to gain an extra two inches.

Did he just ... forget to move? Seriously, that's what it looks like to me. Did he zone out? It sounds like an absurd thing to even think, but this is Cam Skattebo we're talking about. He's a bit out there, if you hadn't noticed.

And don't get me wrong — I love Cam Skattebo. I'm a huge Skattebo guy. I bet on him to score a touchdown last night, so I owe him the whopping $22 I won if I ever see him.

But it was still ... odd. Just odd.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL. First up? Earlier this week, I asked everyone when it was acceptable to put up the Christmas decorations.

Because it's a divisive topic, I received 14,000 responses.

From Greg in Amarillo:

I will put up the Christmas decorations while or when the weather is nice, AFTER Halloween, of course, give them a test light, but they don't get turned on regularly until Thanksgiving weekend. The inside of the house, including the tree, doesn't go up until Thanksgiving weekend.

From Gary B:

When in doubt go old school. As a kid growing up in the 70's everybody would start decorating for Christmas after Thanksgiving. It was corporate greed that tried to change that to Halloween.

From Jon C:

My family tradition is to put up decorations the weekend after Thanksgiving.  Plenty of ballgames to "watch" while decking the halls and trimming the tree (artificial).

And from Chris B:

Hey, Zach — The lights go out on Black Friday, because who wants to leave the house that day anyway? By 5:00 our house looks like a used car lot.

So, I have an admission to make that I'm not proud of ...

Our house is decorated for Christmas. My wife yanked all the Halloween stuff down last weekend (against my wishes), so our house was just in purgatory for days. It wasn't decorated for Halloween. We don't have a ton of fall decor. And there were boxes and bins everywhere.

I couldn't take it anymore. I knew I didn't want to make two trips to the attic, so I decided to bring the Halloween stuff up, and take the Christmas stuff down at the same time.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Once the First Lady caught a whiff of those Christmas bins, it was game over. I didn't stand a chance.

So, we're decking the halls in Florida on Nov. 13. At least we made it to the double-digit portion of November. I held her off as long as I could.

Merry Christmas!

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. On the way out, here's Kansas City Chiefs Heiress Gracie Hunt gearing up for a big game against the Falcons on Sunday.

Have a big weekend, everyone.

item.title: Schumer's leadership rival reveals major Senate rule change he'd pursue if elected
item.description: Chuck Schumer faces a rare contested Senate leadership race as Chris Van Hollen pushes to abolish the filibuster and shake up Democratic strategy.
item.content:encoded:
DENVER — A mile above much of the country, and leagues away from Washington, D.C., Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., is facing a progressive rebellion that threatens his grip on power.

The challenge is being led by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who has served under Schumer since 2017. And he is willing to go further than Schumer ever has on one issue: terminating the filibuster.

Years ago, Schumer tried and failed to narrowly change the Senate’s rule to pass a sweeping voting rights package. Republicans have toyed with it over the last two years, but never pulled the trigger.

SCHUMER'S FORMER ALLY MOUNTS LEADERSHIP CHALLENGE AS DEMOCRATS FACE RARE INTERNAL POWER STRUGGLE

Van Hollen said, "We need democracy in the United States Senate, and that means allowing, ultimately, a majority of senators to answer the call of the American people.

"So, that means 51 votes. So, my personal view has been all along that the filibuster is an anti-democratic … provision. It's not in our Constitution," Van Hollen added. 

"It was put in there by senators to enhance their power over the power of the people."

Van Hollen announced his challenge against Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, Thursday night after a listening campaign with Senate Democrats. It presents a rare opportunity for Senate Democrats since there hasn’t been a contested Democratic leadership election since 1994.

Just a week earlier, Van Hollen was mulling higher office, but now he’s giving up a potential bid for the White House in 2028 to do one thing: beat Schumer and grapple with President Donald Trump.

"I’m no longer pursuing that," Van Hollen told reporters at the What’s Next conference in Denver, where Democratic leaders, strategists and activists gathered to debate the party’s direction after its midterm wins.

Van Hollen framed his challenge to Schumer as a response to voters’ calls for change after Democrats’ sweeping wins and President Donald Trump’s policies.

"I did discuss this with Senator Schumer," Van Hollen told Fox News Digital. "We understand that this will be a competition. I think it’s important to give Senate Democrats a choice."

DEMS ADMIT UNCOMFORTABLE ELECTION SWEEP TRUTH AS PARTY DESCEND ON DENVER TO SHAPE 2028 WITHOUT A FRONTRUNNER

Voters "chose change," he said, adding that the Democratic caucus needs "new ideas" and "a different way of governing."

Van Hollen has also criticized Schumer for limiting votes on legislation popular with Democrats, including a bill to boost unions. He said the incoming majority should pass the bills candidates campaigned on and challenge Trump to respond.

"We shouldn’t wait to hear what President Trump may or may not do," Van Hollen said. "We should answer the call of the American people."

Toppling Schumer will be an uphill climb. As the incumbent leader, he has an established network of support and can offer colleagues leadership posts. 

Either candidate will need 28 votes in the secret ballot contest expected in early December or 29 if Democrats win Alaska, where ballots are still being counted in the Senate race between Democratic nominee Mary Peltola and incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.

THE MISTAKE NEWLY ELECTED DEMS ADMIT THEY CAN’T AFFORD TO MAKE WITH TRUMP AFTER SWEEPING 2026 WINS

Some What’s Next attendees said Van Hollen could deliver the Senate leadership shake-up they want.

"We definitely want change. We don’t want to go back to the way things have been. This is a turning point for our country," Jenny, a Denver resident, said, adding it was time for Schumer to go. 

"This is the time for us to really, really go after what is right for everyone, not the status quo."

Ara, also of Denver, was optimistic about Van Hollen’s chances, saying she believes he already has significant support.

"I think there’s a really good chance," Ara told Fox News Digital. "I think there were a lot of people that were already willing to support him. So I feel very good about this," she added.

Zoe said Van Hollen’s willingness to stand up for his constituents is the kind of fight young people want from their representatives.

"He goes out there, and he puts his body on the line for his constituents. And I think that’s what we’re looking for, the kind of fight we’re looking for from our representatives as young people," Zoe told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Pete Hegseth impeachment effort dies in the House as absent Democrats couldn't beat the traffic
item.description: Pete Hegseth narrowly avoided becoming only the third cabinet secretary ever impeached after 11 absent Democrats failed to reach the House floor.
item.content:encoded:
Most of America bemoans political gridlock in the nation’s capital. DC area commuters deplore the city’s transit gridlock.

But Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth may now be a fan of DC’s legendary traffic snarls. It appears that crosstown traffic may have prevented him from becoming only the third Cabinet secretary ever impeached by the House of Representatives.

The House voted 211-204 this week to divert an effort by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) to impeach Hegseth.

House Republicans moved to block a straight, up-or-down vote on impeachment.

Instead, Republicans forced a vote on sending the articles to the Judiciary Committee.

That’s where they’d go to die. If the House failed to sidetrack the articles, Members would have then voted on actual impeachment.

If a simple majority voted to impeach, Hegseth would join 19th century Secretary of War William Belknap and former Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas as the only Cabinet Members impeached by the House.

But DC’s streetside congestion altered the parliamentary traffic on the House floor.

All Democrats said they were intent on impeaching Hegseth.

But Republicans faced an attendance problem.

Seven of their Members were missing. The vote on sending the impeachment articles to committee was tight. The tally read 204-204 at one point.

By rule, tie votes fail. That would have compelled a vote on actual impeachment. But a few more Republicans trickled in. The absent Democrats never did. Rep. Dan Newhouse (R-Wash.) presided over the vote.

He gaveled it closed at 211 yeas to send the articles to the committee and 204 votes against.

That was it. The Hegseth impeachment quest was dead. Eleven Democrats missed the roll call.

It’s about the math.

Flip four votes and Hegseth would have been impeached, 208-207.

HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT VOTE LOOMS AS HOUSE REPUBLICANS PRIVATELY WARN IT COULD PASS

And, had all 11 truant Democrats made it to the U.S. Capitol and voted, it’s likely the House would have impeached Hegseth 215-211. Even eight Democrats would have made it 212-211.

However, thanks to the Democrats’ attendance issue, Republicans were able to tap the brakes on the impeachment interstate.

The failure to impeach Hegseth is now fueling road rage in the Democratic Party.

"Shame on them for not showing up," said Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda (D-N.C.).

"I don't make excuses for colleagues who don't show up on such an important vote," said Rep. Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.).

Democrats can’t beat Republicans if they can’t beat the traffic.

Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) is one of the most outspoken Democrats when it comes to her disdain for Hegseth.

But Stansbury grew defensive when questioned by colleague Bill Melugin about missing the vote.

"I was trapped right there at that street corner because there was a police motorcade moving busses off of the campus. And I physically was trapped right at that corner in my vehicle, in traffic because the police had shut down traffic," said Stansbury.

"Why not come here sooner, though?" followed up Melugin.

HEGSETH COULD FACE NEW IMPEACHMENT PUSH OVER UKRAINE AID, LAWMAKERS WARN

"I did and I was trapped in my vehicle because of a police motorcade," said Stansbury.

Maybe. Maybe not.

The Constitution’s "Speech or Debate" clause exempts lawmakers from police interference when "going to and from" the Capitol for "their attendance at the Session of their Respective Houses." It’s kind of like diplomatic immunity.

A few years ago, Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.) was supposed to preside over a brief House session in the middle of a recess. Traffic heading into DC from Northern Virginia was stopped because of an incident. Beyer was the only Member scheduled to be present in the House chamber that day. So Beyer identified himself to a police officer who proceeded to let him through.

Over the years, other lawmakers have asserted the Speech or Debate clause as a reason to bypass unrelated police activity and get to Capitol Hill.

Reps. Jonathan Jackson (D-Ill.) and Laura Gillen (D-N.Y.) also said they were stuck in traffic. However, Rep. Lou Correa (D-Calif.) was out for a medical procedure. Rep. Steve Horsford (D-Nev.) missed the vote because of a personal emergency. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) was in the Golden State.

DC’s traffic interfered with parliamentary traffic again on Thursday morning.

The House took an early Thursday morning vote related to a veterans bill.

The House adopted the motion, 271-135. But the House gaveled down the vote with 26 Members absent. The reason? Some Members were again stymied from making it to the Capitol.

Emergency room physician Matt Lambert killed one person at a gym, shot six people and engaged in a standoff with cops before turning the gun on himself. Initially reported as an "active shooter" incident, District of Columbia police locked down major parts of the city, stalling traffic.

And that’s why some lawmakers missed Thursday’s roll call. They were marooned in traffic.

Shifting gears, Rep. Eric Sorensen (D-Ill.) in fact made that procedural vote on the floor. When the vote began, a gentle breeze blew across the Capitol plaza. Then a mist enveloped the Capitol.

Later, a few heavier drops. Then the sun broke through the clouds. But reverted to overcast. It was a dank morning in Washington.

"I want to know what the weather is," yours truly shouted at Sorensen as he skipped down the House steps toward a group of reporters waiting below.

Sorensen is a meteorologist who worked for decades at TV stations in Texas and Illinois before coming to Washington in 2023.

Sorensen pivoted immediately into weatherman mode.

"We've got increasing showers guys. Much cooler temperatures for the weekend," said Sorensen, replicating the precise forecast for Washington, DC over the next few days.

The meteorologist-turned-lawmaker gestured to his right as though looking at a phantom map of the Midwest, projected against a green screen in a TV studio.

"As God is my witness, I cannot talk about the weather without moving my hands," said Sorensen. "I talk about high pressure. It's high pressure right here in the midsection of the country. And it's moving in our direction for the next week."

After the election, the political weather forecast would seem good for Democrats right now. Supposedly balmy days and comfortable nights. A political "high", if you will.

"So is there a high-pressure system moving here for the Democratic Caucus?" yours truly asked.

"No. It's low pressure, man. It's low pressure going into the next Congress. We’ve just got to keep everybody together," he replied.

But is a high-pressure system really in the long-range forecast for Democrats? Or will a political "low" bring storms and atmospheric volatility — especially if progressive and centrist Democrats tangle with one another?

"I thought high pressure was a good thing," said your trusty reporter. "No subtropical systems coming in. No clipper system."

"As a meteorologist, I'm not in production. I'm in promotion," said Sorensen of potential Democratic storm systems which might emerge on the horizon. "With a complicated issue like the weather, I was able to help connect with people every day for 22 years. But here, this is the most complicated mechanism in the United States. We’ve got to get better at communicating what we do for the people."

DC traffic has already stymied Democrats over the past few days. Tornadic political storm systems may brew inside the Democratic Caucus. And that’s to say nothing about transportation and just getting people to the Hill.

Traffic and weather. And if the internal Democratic fisticuffs turn ugly, well, may show that on sports. Right along with the hockey fights.

item.title: Kirk Herbstreit serving steak to his dog at an NYC restaurant has Craig Carton fuming mad
item.description: Kirk Herbstreit fed his golden retriever Peter a steak at an NYC steakhouse, sparking a heated debate over dogs in restaurants and food safety rules.
item.content:encoded:
Has Kirk Herbstreit taken his dog content too far?

On Thursday, Herbstreit's content team bragged across multiple social media channels that Kirk's golden retriever, Peter, "got into another steak in NYC last night," even though it was the football analyst who cut up the steak like he was about to serve it to a six-year-old child.

Go ahead, dog lovers, yell at me: joe.kinsey@outkick.com

"I wish he would enjoy it," Herbstreit, or one of his sons, wrote on social media after the dog ate the steak off a plate on the floor of the unidentified restaurant in 30 seconds.
